name: AWS EC2 G6 / G6e (NVIDIA L4 and L40S, inference-optimized)
region: us-east-1, us-west-2 and most commercial regions
price_basis: per GPU-hour. g6.48xlarge = 8x L4 at $13.3504/instance-hr / 8 = $1.6688. g6e.48xlarge = 8x L40S at $30.13118/8 = $3.7664. g5.48xlarge = 8x A10G at $16.288/8 = $2.036. Single-GPU g6.xlarge = 1x L4 at $0.8048. Fetched 2026-10-03 from the 2026-09-25 offer file; no regional variation found.
notes: THE PRACTICAL INFERENCE FAMILIES on AWS, and the only ones here actually in stock - unlike every p5 record, no $0.00 sentinel appears for g6/g6e and both regions publish real rates. L4 at $1.67/GPU-hr with 24GB is the answer for a small-to-mid model that wants HBM-class bandwidth without Hopper pricing; L40S at $3.77 is the Ada step up with 48GB for models that do not fit. Single-GPU shapes exist and are the sane starting point. Spot applies and AWS advertises up to 90% off on-demand, but I could NOT retrieve a concrete spot rate for these SKUs: the per-instance-type spot table renders client-side and spot-price.s3.amazonaws.com returned HTTP 403. No spot number is recorded here rather than guessing - query describe-spot-price-history before relying on one. AWS's 'up to 40% savings on DL training and HPC infrastructure costs' versus the previous GPU generation is a vendor claim.
